title: How Lemons Changed the History of the World
description:
A small yellow fruit changed the course of world history. Sailors of the Age of Exploration—from Vasco da Gama to Ferdinand Magellan—lost thousands of lives to scurvy, a deadly disease caused by Vitamin C deficiency. Crews bled from gums, lost their teeth, and died slow painful deaths, until lemons and oranges turned out to be the cure. This video traces how citrus fruit went from a sailor’s luxury to the British Navy’s lifesaver, reshaping history itself.

We’ll explore how Sir Richard Hawkins and Sir James Lancaster noticed the benefits of lemon juice, why most ignored the evidence, and how James Lind’s 1747 controlled clinical trial became the first in modern medicine. From James Cook’s voyages with sauerkraut to the British Navy mandating lemon rations, Vitamin C not only conquered scurvy but also changed the balance of naval power, helping Britain dominate the seas.

If you’ve searched for lemons and scurvy, history of Vitamin C, James Lind clinical trial, sailors disease cure, or why the British Navy used lemon juice, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share — hype this video so it reaches more people and sparks better conversations!

Chapters
00:00 – Lemons that changed history
02:10 – The age of voyages and the rise of scurvy
05:20 – Vasco da Gama, Magellan, and mass deaths
09:00 – Early clues: Hawkins, Lancaster, and lemon juice
13:10 – James Lind’s 1747 controlled trial
17:30 – James Cook, sauerkraut, and prevention at sea
21:00 – Navy rations and Britain’s naval dominance
24:00 – What Vitamin C really does in the body
